questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Japan as its one country that has a more significantly different culture than western countries

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was nice to experience the dailylife of Tokyo

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to find the information I neede, though some information like the open courses for USTEP students was difficult to find

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had on two orientations on campus, and other than that there was a center for exchange students, and multiple events

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The global center was open every weekday, where you could ask questions

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Tokyo University supply many housing option, you just have to apply. If I were to apply again though I would choose komaba lodge. I lived at MIV, and even though it was nice, it was also kind of restricted and not that social + komaba lodge is closer to Shibuya

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The subway system is super efficient, and if you manage to find a bicycle that is also an option. 1h transport each way sounds like a lot, but you get used to it, everyone takes the subway.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing I lived at, MIV, was very clean and kind of close to the university

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Tokyo University provide a website with different accomidations that you can apply for

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They are very helpful, and qucik to answer mails.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All kinds of help, they have an office only for dealing with exchange- and international students

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not that successful. I had initially found many relevant courses (chemistry and pharmacy) but when I arrived at the host university I was informed that I could only register for courses open for USTEP students, even though som are in english it can still be closed for USTEP students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just to take alot of chill courses, it does not have to be the semester where you raise your academic knowledge. I had 7 courses, but only one of them with a final exam.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many courses where brand new, with international professors, so at times it was confusing.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As you have 7 courses at a time, the work intensity is high, that being said, the content and expectations are not the highest.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: more classes and less lectures

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Climate repair, invisible connections, modern food resources and consumption, the meaning of language in the age of AI, Humanity and the landscape, bioactive components in food, organic chemistry of natural products

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Climate repair, no matter what field you're in. It's a low effort course, where everybody contributes a final project where you can choose yourself, i chose; Organic chemistry potential to capture GHGs

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected cost, but anticipated high cost of travelling around (Korea, Fukuoka, Hiroshima, Hokkaido etc.)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food, it can be very cheap if you let it. The subway transport was more expensive than I anticipated

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it very hard joining clubs, there is swim lanes and training room on Hongo campus, though the wait for training room introduction was 2-3 months, and you couldn't use it untill then

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I swam a little

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try as much as possible to find a social club, and maybe attend some of the events the global center arranges

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Follow tokyo sites on social media, and just go around and have a look, will recommend sumo tournament, and go for shorter day-trips outside of the city

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very hard! It was exhausting at first, but you adjust graduetly. One thing I wish I had done, was to take a japanese language course

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It's tough, I mainly socialized with other international students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Everything

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cleanliness and silence, just overall a very nice people, but some a very opposed on foreigners

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make an effort to learn japanese phrases, take chill courses, go ski in Hokkaido

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You need to bring cash from home.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just to learn and experience the culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To adjust to the culture and language

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you're looking to only have specific courses in your field of study, this will be hard

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
